cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What are the three fundamental subatomic particles?
cards.answer: Protons, neutrons and electrons. Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons occupy shells, subshells and orbitals around it.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What are the relative charges and masses of protons, neutrons and electrons?
cards.answer: Proton: charge +1, relative mass 1. Neutron: charge 0, relative mass 1. Electron: charge −1, relative mass approximately 1/1836.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What do atomic number and mass number tell you?
cards.answer: Atomic number is the number of protons. Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons. In a neutral atom, electrons equal protons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: How do you calculate the number of neutrons in an atom?
cards.answer: Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What are isotopes?
cards.answer: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What does a time-of-flight mass spectrometer measure?
cards.answer: It measures the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) of ions. Ions are accelerated and their flight times are used to determine m/z.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: How is relative atomic mass calculated from isotopic abundances?
cards.answer: Use the weighted mean: relative atomic mass = Σ(isotopic mass × percentage abundance) ÷ 100.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: How are electrons arranged in atoms?
cards.answer: Electrons occupy shells containing subshells and orbitals. The order of filling follows increasing orbital energy, giving configurations for atoms up to calcium (Z = 20) and beyond.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What are s, p and d subshells and how many electrons can they hold?
cards.answer: An s subshell contains one orbital and holds 2 electrons; a p subshell contains three orbitals and holds 6; a d subshell contains five orbitals and holds 10. Each orbital holds up to 2 electrons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: What is first ionisation energy?
cards.answer: The energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
cards.answer: Nuclear charge increases while shielding changes relatively little. The outer electron is attracted more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove it.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.title: Why are there exceptions to the general first-ionisation-energy trend?
cards.answer: Subshell energy differences and repulsion between paired electrons can make an electron easier to remove at particular points in a period.
